findings.evidence: Diff changes `def discriminantGroupOrthogonalSumEquiv` to `noncomputable def`; the removed `quotientProdLinearEquiv` was computable because `QuotientAddGroup.prodAddEquiv` is (mathlib/Mathlib/GroupTheory/QuotientGroup/Basic.lean:76-85 uses `liftOn'`/`liftOn₂'`, no `Classical.choice`).
findings.fix: Supply the inverse explicitly: `LinearEquiv.ofLinear (quotientProdMap p q) (LinearMap.coprod (p.liftQ ((p.prod q).mkQ ∘ₗ LinearMap.inl R M N) _) (q.liftQ ((p.prod q).mkQ ∘ₗ LinearMap.inr R M N) _)) _ _`, or keep the previous `{ QuotientAddGroup.prodAddEquiv p.toAddSubgroup q.toAddSubgroup with map_smul' := ... }` construction. Then drop `noncomputable` here and at Operations.lean:133.
findings.issue: `quotientProdEquiv` is built by `LinearEquiv.ofBijective`, so its inverse is choice-extracted and opaque; this forces `noncomputable` here and propagates, turning `IntegralLattice.discriminantGroupOrthogonalSumEquiv` from a `def` into a `noncomputable def` (Discriminant/Operations.lean:133) and forcing `quotientProdEquiv_symm_apply_mk` through `LinearEquiv.symm_apply_eq` instead of the map's own computation rule.

findings.evidence: `theorem quot_mk_eq_mk {p : Submodule R M} (x : M) : (Quot.mk _ x : M ⧸ p) = mk x` at mathlib/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Quotient/Defs.lean:71 and `theorem mkQ_apply (x : M) : p.mkQ x = Quotient.mk x` at Defs.lean:233; the deleted proof used `simp only [..., Submodule.mkQ_apply, Submodule.Quotient.quot_mk_eq_mk]`. `Submodule.Quotient.induction_on` is already used in this repo at Discriminant/Operations.lean:164.
findings.fix: Destructure via the API instead of raw `Quot.mk`: `rintro ⟨x, y⟩; induction x using Submodule.Quotient.induction_on with | _ x => induction y using Submodule.Quotient.induction_on with | _ y => exact ⟨Submodule.Quotient.mk (x, y), quotientProdMap_apply_mk p q (x, y)⟩`.
findings.issue: `exact quotientProdMap_apply_mk p q (x, y)` closes the surjectivity goal only through undocumented defeq across two wrappers: `(p.prod q).mkQ (x, y)` vs `Submodule.Quotient.mk (x, y)`, and the `Quot.mk` produced by `rintro ⟨⟨x⟩, ⟨y⟩⟩` vs `Submodule.Quotient.mk`. The proof this replaces bridged both with explicit lemmas (`Submodule.mkQ_apply`, `Submodule.Quotient.quot_mk_eq_mk`).

findings.evidence: `instance : CoeSort (IntegralLattice V) (Type u) := ⟨fun L ↦ L.carrier⟩` at IntegralLattice/Basic.lean:81 with `carrier : Submodule ℤ V` (Basic.lean:63); `orthogonalSum_carrier` is `(rfl)` (OrthogonalSum.lean:95), and line 73 of the same file already applies `Submodule.prodEquiv L.carrier M.carrier` to these types. Pre-diff, `orthogonalSumCarrierEquiv := prodCarrierEquiv L M` with target `L × M`.
findings.fix: Define `orthogonalSumCarrierEquiv L M := Submodule.prodEquiv L.carrier M.carrier` (the removed `prodCarrierEquiv` was used exactly this way) and delete the docstring paragraph.
findings.issue: `orthogonalSumCarrierEquiv` re-inlines `Submodule.prodEquiv` field-for-field (same `toFun`/`invFun`, four `rfl` proofs) in the very PR that extracts that equivalence for reuse, and the docstring justifies it with a claim that does not hold: `↥L` is by definition `↥L.carrier` with the submodule's own ℤ-module structure, so there are no competing module structures.

summary: The extracted quotient equivalence is built with `LinearEquiv.ofBijective`, which discards a computable inverse and turns a previously computable downstream definition noncomputable, and its surjectivity proof crosses two `Quotient.mk` wrappers by bare defeq where the deleted proof used explicit lemmas. `orthogonalSumCarrierEquiv` re-inlines `Submodule.prodEquiv` on a docstring justification that does not hold.
